Date: 2026-11-10

Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Anika Shah (Redwood CSM); Evan Holt, Priya Menon, Marcus Lee, Sofia Duarte (Verdigris)
summary: Check-in focused on contract renewal, activation of an EU geocluster (private VPC option), and a pilot to validate latency and throughput for Verdigris's inference workloads. Customer requested detailed pricing for burst capacity and clarifications on KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, and data residency. Agreed next steps include revised quote, security deep-dive, and a pilot runbook with perf targets.
topics: KMS/HSM and encryption at rest/in transit
transcript:
00:00 Speaker 1 (Maya): Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really appreciate it. quick agenda — renewal numbers, eu geocluster activation, pilot outline.
00:14 Speaker 2 (Evan): Yep thanks Maya, miked. we just want to make sure the capacity bump is in place before jan product freeze, so timeline's tight.
00:28 Speaker 3 (Diego): Awesome, quick note from my side: the geocluster we talked about is essentially private VPC with dedicated nodes, same API surface as hosted but different routing. there might be a short provisioning lead time depending on quota.
00:46 Speaker 4 (Priya): can you clarify lead time? we need to pin dates for infra and network.
00:51 Speaker 3 (Diego): yeah, typically 3-4 weeks once network peering and subnets are approved; if you want on-prem path it's longer, like 6-8 weeks.
01:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): for EU we need data to stay in-region; are you locking residency?
01:11 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes, the plan for geocluster is EU-only routing and storage; we can surface the retention in the contract.
01:20 Speaker 5 (Marcus): on security, KMS integration — are we doing customer-managed keys or do you manage keys? also HSM compliance?
01:27 Speaker 3 (Diego): we support both. customer-managed KMS via your cloud KMS, and we have an HSM-backed offering for private deployments. there are some caveats around key rotation windows and caching for KV caches — small perf trade-offs.
01:45 Speaker 5 (Marcus): caching trade-offs? can you explain?
01:50 Speaker 3 (Diego): sure, when we integrate with an external KMS we cache decrypted keys for the runtime to avoid per-request decrypts. if your security policy forbids caching we can disable it but you'll see higher p50/p95 by a small amount — usually tens of ms.
02:10 Speaker 4 (Priya): tens of ms per token? that's significant at scale.
02:15 Speaker 3 (Diego): yeah it can add about 10-40ms depending on sequence length and model; our recommendation is short cache TTLs with strict audit logging to meet policy and keep perf acceptable.
02:32 Speaker 2 (Evan): on pricing — we need the renewal numbers with explicit burst pricing. last year burst caught us by surprise.
02:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): understood. we'll put line items: base reserved capacity, burst pool (per-minute billing cap), and a buffer for canary traffic. we'll also include estimated token-based cost for your current qps.
02:55 Speaker 6 (Sofia): one more ask — SLA for p99, and what happens during regional failover?
03:03 Speaker 3 (Diego): SLO language — p95 and p99 windows depend on model class; for dedicated geocluster we can guarantee p95 under the commit threshold, p99 is best-effort but we can add higher tiers or fallback to smaller model variants to keep latency bounded. during failover we have automatic routing to fallback region but for EU-only residency you'd have to opt into cross-region fallback in contract.
03:30 Speaker 5 (Marcus): so cross-region fallback is optional; that means during an EU outage our app could be down unless we allow cross-region?
03:36 Speaker 1 (Maya): correct. we can offer a contract clause that permits emergency cross-region routing with audit and double-encryption to satisfy residency controls if needed.
03:50 Speaker 2 (Evan): timeline recap — we need contract signed by Dec 15 to provision before Jan freeze. is that realistic?
03:58 Speaker 1 (Maya): yep, that's doable. we'll deliver a revised quote by Nov 12, you review, legal loop in, sign by Dec 15.
04:10 Speaker 3 (Diego): about the pilot — propose a 48-hour perf window with a ramp to peak qps, we'll run latency p50/p95/p99 and throughput tests against your representative prompts.
04:24 Speaker 6 (Sofia): representative prompts — we'll share a redacted set, but be aware some are longer sequences.
04:30 Speaker 3 (Diego): perfect, sequence length distribution helps us pick quantization and batching configs.
04:36 Speaker 5 (Marcus): logging — what audit fields do you capture? we need user-id, request-id, model-version, timestamp, but not PII.
04:44 Speaker 1 (Maya): yes we can provide structured audit logs; we'll share the network diagram and log schema in the security pack.
04:52 Speaker 2 (Evan): about cost controls — do you support token caps per route or per API key?
04:57 Speaker 3 (Diego): yes, RBAC + per-token quotas; also per-route soft caps that trigger rate-limiters and fallback policies.
05:10 Speaker 6 (Sofia): any mention of competitors — we did talk internally about NimbusCloud, they gave a lower headline price but weaker telemetry.
05:18 Speaker 1 (Maya): good to know. our differentiation is observability and predictable unit economics.
05:24 Speaker 2 (Evan): can you add a sample amortized cost calc for our 2M tokens/day usage?
05:30 Speaker 1 (Maya): will do in the quote.
05:34 Speaker 7 (Unknown - background): (muffled) sorry late to call — question about model pinning.
05:38 Speaker 3 (Diego): model pinning is supported; canary and rollback policies included. if you want automatic fallback to quantized variant we can include that in rollout policy.
05:50 Speaker 6 (Sofia): great. final question — who owns the runbook during the pilot?
05:55 Speaker 3 (Diego): Redwood runs the orchestration and test harness, you provide representative traffic and acceptance criteria. we'll pair on runbook execution.
06:05 Speaker 2 (Evan): ok sounds good. next steps?
06:08 Speaker 1 (Maya): recap — we (Redwood) will: 1) send revised quote w/burst by Nov 12, 2) share SOC2/network/KMS docs and log schema, 3) Diego to draft pilot runbook and perf targets by Nov 22, 4) Anika to prepare onboarding checklist. Customer will send audit list and representative prompt set.
06:28 Speaker 5 (Marcus): i'll send audit list and retention reqs by Nov 17.
06:33 Speaker 6 (Sofia): i'll circulate the redacted prompts today.
06:36 Speaker 2 (Evan): ok thanks, let's aim for the pilot week Nov 24.
06:40 Speaker 1 (Maya): perfect, we'll follow up in email and I'll loop legal. thanks everyone.
06:45 Speaker 3 (Diego): thanks all.
06:47 Speaker 7 (Unknown): bye
06:50 End of recording
